Features.Description: The descriptive name of the product's colour (e.g. Space Grey).
The sub-category of the product.
The colour e.g. red, blue, green, black, white.
The shape or design of the product.
Under which category can the device be positioned in the market, e.g. camera phone.
The calendar year in which the product was first released or introduced to the market.
Size of the display for this product, measured diagonally, usually in inches.

The number of distinct pixels in each dimension that can be displayed. It is usually quoted as width × height, with the units in pixels: for example, "1024 × 768" means the width is 1024 pixels and the height is 768 pixels. The higher the number of pixels, the sharper the image.
A screen of a laptop, smartphone, etc., that responds to touch so you can control the interface using your fingers.
Type of supported High Definition (e.g. Full HD, 4K Ultra HD).
The technology used to manufacture the panel, such as AMOLED or AH-IPS.

The aspect ratio is the ratio of the width of an image to its height. The native aspect ratio is the one which the projector/display is particularly designed for. Images shown in native aspect ratio will utilize the entire resolution of the display and achieve maximum brightness. Images shown in other than native aspect ratio will always have less resolution and less brightness than images shown in native aspect ratio.
Always gives an optimal view, even in direct sunlight.
The specific color gamut standard the display is capable of reproducing (e.g. sRGB or Adobe RGB).
The range of colours that the display can accurately reproduce, typically expressed as a percentage of a standard colour space (e.g. sRGB or Adobe RGB).
The highest number of times per second the image is updated, measured in hertz (Hz).
The manufacturer that produced the processor.
A family of processors is a group of processors produced by one company over a short period of time e.g. Intel Pentium processors.
The specific architectural version or series of the processor (e.g. 7th Gen).
The model number for the processor in a computer.
The number of central processing units ('cores') in a processor. Some processors have 1 core, others have 2 (e.g. Intel Core Duo) or more (e.g. the Intel Xeon E7-2850 has 10 cores).
The number of virtual cores available for simultaneous processing tasks (e.g. 12 or 128).
The turbo boost is an automatic, managed accelleration of the processor when one of the cores is overloaded.

The speed that the microprocessor executes each instruction or each vibration of the clock. The CPU requires a fixed number of clock ticks, or cycles, to execute each instruction. The faster the clocks rate, the faster the CPU, or the faster it can execute instructions. Clock Speeds are usually determined in MHz, 1 MHz representing 1 million cycles per second, or in GHz, 1 GHz representing 1 thousand million cycles per second. The higher the CPU speed, the better a computer will perform.
The architecture level or specific technology of the high-speed memory integrated into the processor (e.g., L2 or Smart Cache).
The amount of level 3 memory available to the processor for high-speed data access, typically measured in megabytes (MB).
The CPU cache (Level 2) is a smaller, faster memory which stores copies of the data from the most frequently used main memory locations.
A computer's memory which is directly accessible to the CPU.
The type of internal memory such as RAM, GDDR5.
The frequency at which the memory (e.g. RAM) runs.
Design of the memory e.g. 240-pin DIMM, SO-DIMM.
Number and type of memory expansion slots, including connector and memory module descriptions.
The maximum internal memory which is available in the product.
The number of communication paths between the memory controller and the RAM, which affects data transfer bandwidth (e.g., Dual-channel).
The total amount of data that can be stored on the device.
Used for the storage of data e.g. HDD (hard disk drive), SSD (solid-state drive).
The combined storage space of all installed solid state drives, typically measured in gigabytes (GB) or terabytes (TB).
The total quantity of solid state drives integrated into the device.
The Solid State Drive's data storage capacity.
The type of interface(s) with which the Solid State Drive is connected to other hardware.

NVM Express (NVMe) or Non-Volatile Memory Host Controller Interface Specification (NVMHCIS) is an open logical device interface specification for accessing non-volatile storage media attached via a PCI Express (PCIe) bus. NVM Express, as a logical device interface, has been designed to capitalize on the low latency and internal parallelism of solid-state storage devices.
The size of the solid-state drive, given in inches
An optical drive uses laser to read optical discs such as CDs, DVDs and Blu-Ray. Some types of optical drive are: CD ROM drive, CR-RW (CD writer) drive, DVD-ROM.
A card reader is a device that enables reading and, in some cases, writing data to and from a memory card.
The company that produced the dedicated graphics processing unit (e.g. NVIDIA, AMD, Intel).

A graphics adapter (often known as a video card) generates images for a display. A discrete graphics adapter plugs into the motherboard, and usually produces much better graphics than an integrated graphics adapter. There are various models of discrete graphics adapters.
The amount of dedicated video RAM (VRAM) available on the separate graphics processing unit, measured in gigabytes (GB).
The specific generation and standard of memory used by the dedicated graphics processor (e.g. GDDR6).
Graphics hardware which is built into the motherboard or CPU, as opposed to a separate graphics adapter (video card). On-board graphics uses CPU and RAM for graphics processing.
The company that designed and produced the integrated graphics processing unit (e.g. Intel, AMD, NVIDIA).
Indicates whether the device has a dedicated graphics processor separate from the main CPU.
The specific series or generation of the integrated graphics (e.g. AMD Radeon Graphics).
"Graphic adapter" is the hardware that produces images on a display. "On-board" means that the graphics adapter is intergrated inside the motherboard.
Indicates whether the product supports NVIDIA G-SYNC technology to synchronize the display refresh rate with the GPU to eliminate screen tearing.
System used to play music or speech.
The total quantity of integrated audio output drivers installed within the unit.
Microphone that is found inside the product.
Camera at the front of the product.
The maximum resolution supported by the front-facing camera (e.g., Full HD or Ultra HD).
Indicates whether the device is equipped with an infrared camera, typically used for facial recognition and biometric security.
Connection of this device is done via Wi-Fi in a high standard.

The type of wireless local area network (LAN). It can be ad-hoc, where units in a network communicate peer-to-peer, or Infrastructure, where units communicate with each other via an access point  A LAN interconnects computers in a small area e.g. home, school or office.
Indicates whether the device has built-in hardware to connect to cellular data networks.
Type of antenna, also known an aerial, e.g. external, internal.
An Ethernet LAN (Local Area Network) interface is present, for a wired conection via a cable.
The different speed levels of the Ethernet LAN connection.

Bluetooth is a low-power radio technology developed to replace the cables and wires currently used to link or connect electronic devices such as personal computers, printers, and a wide variety of handheld devices including mobile phones. Because it uses radio-wave connectivity, a Bluetooth-enabled device has a constant, established connection to whatever browser it uses. This saves the user the trouble of logging on to check for emails or news updates, for example.
The type of bluetooth technology in the product e.g. Bluetooth Smart (v4.0).
The total number of USB Type-A ports that support the 3.2 Gen 2 (formerly 3.1 Gen 2) standard for high-speed data transfer.

Name.Value: USB 3.2 Gen 2 (3.1 Gen 2) Type-A ports quantity

Features.Description: Number of USB 3.1 (3.1 Gen 2) ports with Type-C connector. USB 3.1 (3.1 Gen 2) is USB interface version which supports transfer rate up to 10 Gbit/s (SuperSpeed+). USB Type-C connector has symmetrical design architecture and compatible with Thunderbolt 3 interface.

Name.Value: USB 3.2 Gen 2 (3.1 Gen 2) Type-C ports quantity

Features.Description: Number of Ethernet LAN (RJ-45) ports (connecting interfaces) in the device.  Ethernet LAN (RJ-45) ports allow a computer to connect to the ethernet.

The number of sockets (ports) for HDMI connections. HDMI (High-Definition Multimedia Interface) is a compact audio/video interface for transferring uncompressed video data and compressed/uncompressed digital audio data from a HDMI-compliant device ("the source device") to a compatible computer monitor, video projector, digital television, or digital audio device. HDMI is a digital replacement for existing analog video standards.
The specific release version of the High-Definition Multimedia Interface standard supported by the device (e.g. 1.3 or 2.0).
Indicates whether the device features a single integrated jack that supports both audio output for headphones and audio input for a microphone.
Indicates whether the USB Type-C port supports the transmission of native DisplayPort video signals to an external display.
The type of integrated input mechanism used to control the cursor (e.g., Clickpad or DialPad).

Small, palm-sized, seventeen key section of a computer keyboard, usually on the very far right. The numeric keypad features digits 0 to 9, addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (*) and division (/) symbols, a decimal point (.) and Num Lock and Enter keys. Laptop keyboards often do not have a numpad, but may provide numpad input by holding a modifier key (typically labelled "Fn") and operating keys on the standard keyboard.
Indicates whether the device features integrated illumination to improve visibility in low-light conditions.
The available color or lighting mode of the illumination beneath the keyboard keys (e.g. RGB).
Specifies the configuration of the illumination areas under the keys, such as individual per-key RGB or divided into multiple sections (e.g. 3-zone RGB).
Indicates whether the device features a dedicated hardware key to launch the AI assistant.
Type of operating system on a device e.g. IOS on Apple devices, Android for mobile devices.
The type of battery in the device, e.g. nickel–cadmium (NiCd).
The total quantity of individual battery cells used to power the device, including configurations with primary and backup cells (e.g., 1+2).
A measure of the charge stored by the battery. Determined by the mass of active material contained in the battery.
Indicates whether the product supports a high-current charging standard to reduce the time required for a full charge.
The time required to charge the battery from zero to 50% capacity, measured in min.
The maximum power output provided by the AC adapter, measured in watts (e.g. 65 W).
The alternating current frequency range or specific value required by the power supply, measured in hertz (e.g., 50/60).
The range of alternating current voltage that the power supply can safely accept from a wall outlet, measured in volts (e.g., 100-240).
The maximum electrical current supplied by the power adapter, measured in amperes (A).
The electrical potential difference supplied by the power adapter to the device, measured in volts (e.g. 19).
The socket/plug where the DC electricity supply connects to the device.
Indicates whether the product features a USB Type-C port specifically for charging purposes.
Indicates whether the device supports the USB Power Delivery standard for faster charging and higher power levels.
Indicates whether the device supports biometric authentication via facial scanning for secure access.
Indicates whether the device supports Windows Hello for passwordless authentication via biometric verification or a PIN.

The measurement or extent of something from side to side.
The distance from the front to the back of something.
The measurement of the product from head to foot or from base to top.

Weight of the product without packaging (net weight). If possible, the net weight is given including standard accessories and supplies. Please note that sometimes the manufacturer leaves out the weight of accessories and/or supplies.
Indicates whether a power supply unit for connecting the device to an AC outlet is provided in the package.
The length of time the manufacturer guarantees the product against defects, typically expressed in months or years.

The sub-category of the product.
The colour e.g. red, blue, green, black, white.
The shape or design of the product.
What the casing of the product is made of.
Size of the display for this product, measured diagonally, usually in inches.

The number of distinct pixels in each dimension that can be displayed. It is usually quoted as width × height, with the units in pixels: for example, "1024 × 768" means the width is 1024 pixels and the height is 768 pixels. The higher the number of pixels, the sharper the image.
A screen of a laptop, smartphone, etc., that responds to touch so you can control the interface using your fingers.
Type of supported High Definition (e.g. Full HD, 4K Ultra HD).

A backlight is a form of illumination used in liquid crystal displays (LCDs). One type of backlight is made by LEDs, which can be either white or RGB (red green blue). White LEDs are used most often in notebooks and desktop screens, and in virtually all mobile LCD screens. RGB LEDs for backlighting are found in high-end color proofing displays such as HP DreamColor LP2480zx monitor or selected HP EliteBook notebooks, as well as newer consumer grade displays such as Dell's Studio series laptops which have an optional RGB LED display.

The aspect ratio is the ratio of the width of an image to its height. The native aspect ratio is the one which the projector/display is particularly designed for. Images shown in native aspect ratio will utilize the entire resolution of the display and achieve maximum brightness. Images shown in other than native aspect ratio will always have less resolution and less brightness than images shown in native aspect ratio.
The specific color gamut standard the display is capable of reproducing (e.g. sRGB or Adobe RGB).
The range of colours that the display can accurately reproduce, typically expressed as a percentage of a standard colour space (e.g. sRGB or Adobe RGB).
Indicates whether the device supports High Dynamic Range for improved contrast and a wider range of colours and luminosity.
The specific standard or version of high contrast and color reproduction used to enhance the detail in the darkest and brightest areas of an image (e.g. DisplayHDR 600).
The manufacturer that produced the processor.
A family of processors is a group of processors produced by one company over a short period of time e.g. Intel Pentium processors.
The specific architectural version or series of the processor (e.g. 7th Gen).
The model number for the processor in a computer.
The number of central processing units ('cores') in a processor. Some processors have 1 core, others have 2 (e.g. Intel Core Duo) or more (e.g. the Intel Xeon E7-2850 has 10 cores).
The number of virtual cores available for simultaneous processing tasks (e.g. 12 or 128).
The turbo boost is an automatic, managed accelleration of the processor when one of the cores is overloaded.

The speed that the microprocessor executes each instruction or each vibration of the clock. The CPU requires a fixed number of clock ticks, or cycles, to execute each instruction. The faster the clocks rate, the faster the CPU, or the faster it can execute instructions. Clock Speeds are usually determined in MHz, 1 MHz representing 1 million cycles per second, or in GHz, 1 GHz representing 1 thousand million cycles per second. The higher the CPU speed, the better a computer will perform.
The architecture level or specific technology of the high-speed memory integrated into the processor (e.g., L2 or Smart Cache).
The amount of level 3 memory available to the processor for high-speed data access, typically measured in megabytes (MB).
The CPU cache (Level 2) is a smaller, faster memory which stores copies of the data from the most frequently used main memory locations.
A computer's memory which is directly accessible to the CPU.
The type of internal memory such as RAM, GDDR5.
The frequency at which the memory (e.g. RAM) runs.
Design of the memory e.g. 240-pin DIMM, SO-DIMM.
Number and type of memory expansion slots, including connector and memory module descriptions.
The maximum internal memory which is available in the product.
The number of communication paths between the memory controller and the RAM, which affects data transfer bandwidth (e.g., Dual-channel).
The total amount of data that can be stored on the device.
Used for the storage of data e.g. HDD (hard disk drive), SSD (solid-state drive).
The combined storage space of all installed solid state drives, typically measured in gigabytes (GB) or terabytes (TB).
The total quantity of solid state drives integrated into the device.
The Solid State Drive's data storage capacity.
The type of interface(s) with which the Solid State Drive is connected to other hardware.

NVM Express (NVMe) or Non-Volatile Memory Host Controller Interface Specification (NVMHCIS) is an open logical device interface specification for accessing non-volatile storage media attached via a PCI Express (PCIe) bus. NVM Express, as a logical device interface, has been designed to capitalize on the low latency and internal parallelism of solid-state storage devices.
The size of the solid-state drive, given in inches
The physical dimensions of the module, where the first two digits represent the width and the remaining digits represent the length in millimetres (e.g. 2280 for 22 x 80 mm).
An optical drive uses laser to read optical discs such as CDs, DVDs and Blu-Ray. Some types of optical drive are: CD ROM drive, CR-RW (CD writer) drive, DVD-ROM.
A card reader is a device that enables reading and, in some cases, writing data to and from a memory card.
The company that produced the dedicated graphics processing unit (e.g. NVIDIA, AMD, Intel).

A graphics adapter (often known as a video card) generates images for a display. A discrete graphics adapter plugs into the motherboard, and usually produces much better graphics than an integrated graphics adapter. There are various models of discrete graphics adapters.
The amount of dedicated video RAM (VRAM) available on the separate graphics processing unit, measured in gigabytes (GB).
The specific generation and standard of memory used by the dedicated graphics processor (e.g. GDDR6).
Graphics hardware which is built into the motherboard or CPU, as opposed to a separate graphics adapter (video card). On-board graphics uses CPU and RAM for graphics processing.
The company that designed and produced the integrated graphics processing unit (e.g. Intel, AMD, NVIDIA).
Indicates whether the device has a dedicated graphics processor separate from the main CPU.
The specific series or generation of the integrated graphics (e.g. AMD Radeon Graphics).
"Graphic adapter" is the hardware that produces images on a display. "On-board" means that the graphics adapter is intergrated inside the motherboard.
Indicates whether the product supports NVIDIA G-SYNC technology to synchronize the display refresh rate with the GPU to eliminate screen tearing.
The product includes AMD Freesync Technology for the dynamic synchronization of the graphic card and the monitor in order to avoid screen tearing.
The specific integrated circuit or hardware component responsible for processing audio signals (e.g., ALC3287-CGT).
System used to play music or speech.
The total quantity of integrated audio output drivers installed within the unit.
The brand responsible for the design and production of the integrated speakers (e.g. Bang & Olufsen or Harman Kardon).
The electrical power output delivered to the audio output components, typically measured in Watts (W).
Microphone that is found inside the product.
The total quantity of integrated microphones built into the device.
Camera at the front of the product.
The maximum number of pixels captured by the front-facing sensor, typically expressed in megapixels.
Indicates whether the device features a physical shutter or cover to block the camera lens for enhanced privacy.
Connection of this device is done via Wi-Fi in a high standard.

The type of wireless local area network (LAN). It can be ad-hoc, where units in a network communicate peer-to-peer, or Infrastructure, where units communicate with each other via an access point  A LAN interconnects computers in a small area e.g. home, school or office.
Indicates whether the device has built-in hardware to connect to cellular data networks.
Type of antenna, also known an aerial, e.g. external, internal.
An Ethernet LAN (Local Area Network) interface is present, for a wired conection via a cable.
The different speed levels of the Ethernet LAN connection.

Bluetooth is a low-power radio technology developed to replace the cables and wires currently used to link or connect electronic devices such as personal computers, printers, and a wide variety of handheld devices including mobile phones. Because it uses radio-wave connectivity, a Bluetooth-enabled device has a constant, established connection to whatever browser it uses. This saves the user the trouble of logging on to check for emails or news updates, for example.
The type of bluetooth technology in the product e.g. Bluetooth Smart (v4.0).
Indicates the availability of a wireless wide area network module for cellular data connectivity (e.g. Installed, Not installed, or Upgradable).
The total number of available USB 3.2 Gen 1 (formerly 3.1 Gen 1) Type-A connection ports on the device.

Name.Value: USB 3.2 Gen 1 (3.1 Gen 1) Type-A ports quantity

Name.Value: USB 3.2 Gen 2 (3.1 Gen 2) Type-A ports quantity

Features.Description: Number of USB 3.1 (3.1 Gen 2) ports with Type-C connector. USB 3.1 (3.1 Gen 2) is USB interface version which supports transfer rate up to 10 Gbit/s (SuperSpeed+). USB Type-C connector has symmetrical design architecture and compatible with Thunderbolt 3 interface.

Name.Value: USB 3.2 Gen 2 (3.1 Gen 2) Type-C ports quantity

Features.Description: Number of Ethernet LAN (RJ-45) ports (connecting interfaces) in the device.  Ethernet LAN (RJ-45) ports allow a computer to connect to the ethernet.

The number of sockets (ports) for HDMI connections. HDMI (High-Definition Multimedia Interface) is a compact audio/video interface for transferring uncompressed video data and compressed/uncompressed digital audio data from a HDMI-compliant device ("the source device") to a compatible computer monitor, video projector, digital television, or digital audio device. HDMI is a digital replacement for existing analog video standards.
The specific release version of the High-Definition Multimedia Interface standard supported by the device (e.g. 1.3 or 2.0).

Indicates whether the device has a USB port that can charge external peripherals even while the system is in sleep mode.

The type of integrated input mechanism used to control the cursor (e.g., Clickpad or DialPad).

Small, palm-sized, seventeen key section of a computer keyboard, usually on the very far right. The numeric keypad features digits 0 to 9, addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (*) and division (/) symbols, a decimal point (.) and Num Lock and Enter keys. Laptop keyboards often do not have a numpad, but may provide numpad input by holding a modifier key (typically labelled "Fn") and operating keys on the standard keyboard.

Indicates whether the product features a USB Type-C port specifically for charging purposes.
The minimum power delivery required from a USB Type-C power source to charge the device, measured in watts (e.g. 18 W).
The maximum electrical power required by the device for charging via a USB Type-C connection, measured in watts.
Indicates whether the device supports the USB Power Delivery standard for faster charging and higher power levels.

The specific release version of the High-Definition Multimedia Interface standard supported by the device (e.g. 1.3 or 2.0).
Indicates whether the device features a single integrated jack that supports both audio output for headphones and audio input for a microphone.
Indicates whether the USB Type-C port supports the transmission of native DisplayPort video signals to an external display.
The type of integrated input mechanism used to control the cursor (e.g., Clickpad or DialPad).

Small, palm-sized, seventeen key section of a computer keyboard, usually on the very far right. The numeric keypad features digits 0 to 9, addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (*) and division (/) symbols, a decimal point (.) and Num Lock and Enter keys. Laptop keyboards often do not have a numpad, but may provide numpad input by holding a modifier key (typically labelled "Fn") and operating keys on the standard keyboard.
Indicates whether the device features integrated illumination to improve visibility in low-light conditions.

The number of virtual cores available for simultaneous processing tasks (e.g. 12 or 128).
The turbo boost is an automatic, managed accelleration of the processor when one of the cores is overloaded.

The speed that the microprocessor executes each instruction or each vibration of the clock. The CPU requires a fixed number of clock ticks, or cycles, to execute each instruction. The faster the clocks rate, the faster the CPU, or the faster it can execute instructions. Clock Speeds are usually determined in MHz, 1 MHz representing 1 million cycles per second, or in GHz, 1 GHz representing 1 thousand million cycles per second. The higher the CPU speed, the better a computer will perform.
The number of high-performance cores designed to handle demanding tasks and heavy workloads.
The number of high-efficiency processor cores designed to handle background tasks and power-saving operations.
The maximum clock speed that the high-performance cores can reach during intensive tasks, measured in gigahertz (GHz).
The maximum clock speed that the efficiency cores can reach during peak demand, measured in gigahertz (GHz).
The guaranteed minimum clock speed of the high-performance processor cores, measured in megahertz (MHz) or gigahertz (GHz).
The minimum clock speed at which the efficiency cores of the processor operate, measured in megahertz (MHz) or gigahertz (GHz).
The amount of high-speed volatile memory integrated into the processor to reduce the average time to access data from the main memory, typically measured in megabytes (MB).
The architecture level or specific technology of the high-speed memory integrated into the processor (e.g., L2 or Smart Cache).
The minimum amount of power the processor is designed to consume during normal operation, measured in watts.
The highest power consumption level the processor can reach during peak performance bursts, measured in watts.
A computer's memory which is directly accessible to the CPU.
The type of internal memory such as RAM, GDDR5.
The frequency at which the memory (e.g. RAM) runs.
Design of the memory e.g. 240-pin DIMM, SO-DIMM.
The slots and size of the memory for the CPU.
Number and type of memory expansion slots, including connector and memory module descriptions.
The maximum internal memory which is available in the product.
The total amount of data that can be stored on the device.
Used for the storage of data e.g. HDD (hard disk drive), SSD (solid-state drive).
The combined storage space of all installed solid state drives, typically measured in gigabytes (GB) or terabytes (TB).
The total quantity of solid state drives integrated into the device.
The Solid State Drive's data storage capacity.
The type of interface(s) with which the Solid State Drive is connected to other hardware.

NVM Express (NVMe) or Non-Volatile Memory Host Controller Interface Specification (NVMHCIS) is an open logical device interface specification for accessing non-volatile storage media attached via a PCI Express (PCIe) bus. NVM Express, as a logical device interface, has been designed to capitalize on the low latency and internal parallelism of solid-state storage devices.
The size of the solid-state drive, given in inches
An optical drive uses laser to read optical discs such as CDs, DVDs and Blu-Ray. Some types of optical drive are: CD ROM drive, CR-RW (CD writer) drive, DVD-ROM.
A card reader is a device that enables reading and, in some cases, writing data to and from a memory card.
The company that produced the dedicated graphics processing unit (e.g. NVIDIA, AMD, Intel).

A graphics adapter (often known as a video card) generates images for a display. A discrete graphics adapter plugs into the motherboard, and usually produces much better graphics than an integrated graphics adapter. There are various models of discrete graphics adapters.
The amount of dedicated video RAM (VRAM) available on the separate graphics processing unit, measured in gigabytes (GB).
The specific generation and standard of memory used by the dedicated graphics processor (e.g. GDDR6).
Graphics hardware which is built into the motherboard or CPU, as opposed to a separate graphics adapter (video card). On-board graphics uses CPU and RAM for graphics processing.
The company that designed and produced the integrated graphics processing unit (e.g. Intel, AMD, NVIDIA).
Indicates whether the device has a dedicated graphics processor separate from the main CPU.
The specific series or generation of the integrated graphics (e.g. AMD Radeon Graphics).
"Graphic adapter" is the hardware that produces images on a display. "On-board" means that the graphics adapter is intergrated inside the motherboard.
The specific integrated circuit or hardware component responsible for processing audio signals (e.g., ALC3287-CGT).
The total quantity of integrated audio output drivers installed within the unit.
The electrical power output delivered to the audio output components, typically measured in Watts (W).
Microphone that is found inside the product.
The total quantity of integrated microphones built into the device.
The maximum number of pixels captured by the front-facing sensor, typically expressed in megapixels.
Indicates whether the device features a physical shutter or cover to block the camera lens for enhanced privacy.
The mechanism used to physically or electronically disable the image or audio capture for security and privacy (e.g. privacy shutter, kill switch).
Connection of this device is done via Wi-Fi in a high standard.

The type of wireless local area network (LAN). It can be ad-hoc, where units in a network communicate peer-to-peer, or Infrastructure, where units communicate with each other via an access point  A LAN interconnects computers in a small area e.g. home, school or office.
Indicates whether the device has built-in hardware to connect to cellular data networks.
Type of antenna, also known an aerial, e.g. external, internal.
An Ethernet LAN (Local Area Network) interface is present, for a wired conection via a cable.
The different speed levels of the Ethernet LAN connection.

Bluetooth is a low-power radio technology developed to replace the cables and wires currently used to link or connect electronic devices such as personal computers, printers, and a wide variety of handheld devices including mobile phones. Because it uses radio-wave connectivity, a Bluetooth-enabled device has a constant, established connection to whatever browser it uses. This saves the user the trouble of logging on to check for emails or news updates, for example.
The type of bluetooth technology in the product e.g. Bluetooth Smart (v4.0).
Indicates the availability of a wireless wide area network module for cellular data connectivity (e.g. Installed, Not installed, or Upgradable).
The total number of available USB 3.2 Gen 1 (formerly 3.1 Gen 1) Type-A connection ports on the device.

Name.Value: USB 3.2 Gen 2 (3.1 Gen 2) Type-C ports quantity

The number of sockets (ports) for HDMI connections. HDMI (High-Definition Multimedia Interface) is a compact audio/video interface for transferring uncompressed video data and compressed/uncompressed digital audio data from a HDMI-compliant device ("the source device") to a compatible computer monitor, video projector, digital television, or digital audio device. HDMI is a digital replacement for existing analog video standards.
The specific release version of the High-Definition Multimedia Interface standard supported by the device (e.g. 1.3 or 2.0).
Indicates whether the device features a single integrated jack that supports both audio output for headphones and audio input for a microphone.

The chipset connects the microprocessor to the rest of the motherboard.
The type of integrated input mechanism used to control the cursor (e.g., Clickpad or DialPad).

Small, palm-sized, seventeen key section of a computer keyboard, usually on the very far right. The numeric keypad features digits 0 to 9, addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (*) and division (/) symbols, a decimal point (.) and Num Lock and Enter keys. Laptop keyboards often do not have a numpad, but may provide numpad input by holding a modifier key (typically labelled "Fn") and operating keys on the standard keyboard.
Indicates whether the device features integrated illumination to improve visibility in low-light conditions.
The available color or lighting mode of the illumination beneath the keyboard keys (e.g. RGB).
Specifies the configuration of the illumination areas under the keys, such as individual per-key RGB or divided into multiple sections (e.g. 3-zone RGB).
The letters which are marked on the keys for convenience of the keyboard usage with specific language.
Type of operating system on a device e.g. IOS on Apple devices, Android for mobile devices.
A measure of the charge stored by the battery. Determined by the mass of active material contained in the battery.

Indicates whether the product features a USB Type-C port specifically for charging purposes.
Indicates whether the device supports the USB Power Delivery standard for faster charging and higher power levels.

A scanner used to identify a person's fingerprint for security purposes. After a sample is taken, access to a computer or other system is granted if the fingerprint matches the stored sample. A PIN may also be used with the fingerprint sample.

The maximum processing power of the Neural Processing Unit, typically measured in trillions of operations per second (TOPS).
The maximum theoretical computing power of the graphics processing unit, measured in TOPs.
A computer's memory which is directly accessible to the CPU.
The type of internal memory such as RAM, GDDR5.
The frequency at which the memory (e.g. RAM) runs.
The slots and size of the memory for the CPU.
Number and type of memory expansion slots, including connector and memory module descriptions.
The maximum internal memory which is available in the product.
The total amount of data that can be stored on the device.
Used for the storage of data e.g. HDD (hard disk drive), SSD (solid-state drive).
The combined storage space of all installed solid state drives, typically measured in gigabytes (GB) or terabytes (TB).
The total quantity of solid state drives integrated into the device.
The Solid State Drive's data storage capacity.
The type of interface(s) with which the Solid State Drive is connected to other hardware.

NVM Express (NVMe) or Non-Volatile Memory Host Controller Interface Specification (NVMHCIS) is an open logical device interface specification for accessing non-volatile storage media attached via a PCI Express (PCIe) bus. NVM Express, as a logical device interface, has been designed to capitalize on the low latency and internal parallelism of solid-state storage devices.
The size of the solid-state drive, given in inches
The physical dimensions of the module, where the first two digits represent the width and the remaining digits represent the length in millimetres (e.g. 2280 for 22 x 80 mm).
An optical drive uses laser to read optical discs such as CDs, DVDs and Blu-Ray. Some types of optical drive are: CD ROM drive, CR-RW (CD writer) drive, DVD-ROM.
A card reader is a device that enables reading and, in some cases, writing data to and from a memory card.
Types of memory cards which can be used with this product.
The company that produced the dedicated graphics processing unit (e.g. NVIDIA, AMD, Intel).

Features.Description: A graphics adapter (often known as a video card) generates images for a display. A discrete graphics adapter plugs into the motherboard, and usually produces much better graphics than an integrated graphics adapter. There are various models of discrete graphics adapters.
The amount of dedicated video RAM (VRAM) available on the separate graphics processing unit, measured in gigabytes (GB).
The specific generation and standard of memory used by the dedicated graphics processor (e.g. GDDR6).
Graphics hardware which is built into the motherboard or CPU, as opposed to a separate graphics adapter (video card). On-board graphics uses CPU and RAM for graphics processing.
The company that designed and produced the integrated graphics processing unit (e.g. Intel, AMD, NVIDIA).
Indicates whether the device has a dedicated graphics processor separate from the main CPU.
The specific series or generation of the integrated graphics (e.g. AMD Radeon Graphics).
"Graphic adapter" is the hardware that produces images on a display. "On-board" means that the graphics adapter is intergrated inside the motherboard.
System used to play music or speech.
The total quantity of integrated audio output drivers installed within the unit.
The electrical power output delivered to the audio output components, typically measured in Watts (W).
Camera at the front of the product.
The maximum number of pixels captured by the forward-facing sensor, typically expressed as width by height (e.g. 1280 x 720).
The maximum resolution supported by the front-facing camera (e.g., Full HD or Ultra HD).
The maximum number of frames per second (fps) that the device can record during video capture.
Indicates whether the device is equipped with an infrared camera, typically used for facial recognition and biometric security.
Indicates whether the device features a physical shutter or cover to block the camera lens for enhanced privacy.
The mechanism used to physically or electronically disable the image or audio capture for security and privacy (e.g. privacy shutter, kill switch).
Connection of this device is done via Wi-Fi in a high standard.

The type of wireless local area network (LAN). It can be ad-hoc, where units in a network communicate peer-to-peer, or Infrastructure, where units communicate with each other via an access point  A LAN interconnects computers in a small area e.g. home, school or office.
Indicates whether the device has built-in hardware to connect to cellular data networks.
The specific model or chipset of the integrated wireless network adapter (e.g. AMD RZ608).
The company that designed and produced the wireless network interface controller (e.g. Intel, Qualcomm, Realtek).
An Ethernet LAN (Local Area Network) interface is present, for a wired conection via a cable.
The different speed levels of the Ethernet LAN connection.

Bluetooth is a low-power radio technology developed to replace the cables and wires currently used to link or connect electronic devices such as personal computers, printers, and a wide variety of handheld devices including mobile phones. Because it uses radio-wave connectivity, a Bluetooth-enabled device has a constant, established connection to whatever browser it uses. This saves the user the trouble of logging on to check for emails or news updates, for example.
The type of bluetooth technology in the product e.g. Bluetooth Smart (v4.0).
The total number of USB Type-A ports that support the 3.2 Gen 2 (formerly 3.1 Gen 2) standard for high-speed data transfer.

Name.Value: USB 3.2 Gen 2 (3.1 Gen 2) Type-A ports quantity

Features.Description: Number of Ethernet LAN (RJ-45) ports (connecting interfaces) in the device.  Ethernet LAN (RJ-45) ports allow a computer to connect to the ethernet.

The number of sockets (ports) for HDMI connections. HDMI (High-Definition Multimedia Interface) is a compact audio/video interface for transferring uncompressed video data and compressed/uncompressed digital audio data from a HDMI-compliant device ("the source device") to a compatible computer monitor, video projector, digital television, or digital audio device. HDMI is a digital replacement for existing analog video standards.
The specific release version of the High-Definition Multimedia Interface standard supported by the device (e.g. 1.3 or 2.0).
The total number of Thunderbolt 5 interface ports available on the device.
Indicates whether the device supports the Intel Thunderbolt 5 interface for high-speed data transfer and connectivity.
Indicates whether the device features a single integrated jack that supports both audio output for headphones and audio input for a microphone.
The chipset connects the microprocessor to the rest of the motherboard.
The type of integrated input mechanism used to control the cursor (e.g., Clickpad or DialPad).

Small, palm-sized, seventeen key section of a computer keyboard, usually on the very far right. The numeric keypad features digits 0 to 9, addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (*) and division (/) symbols, a decimal point (.) and Num Lock and Enter keys. Laptop keyboards often do not have a numpad, but may provide numpad input by holding a modifier key (typically labelled "Fn") and operating keys on the standard keyboard.
Indicates whether the device features integrated illumination to improve visibility in low-light conditions.
The available color or lighting mode of the illumination beneath the keyboard keys (e.g. RGB).
Specifies the configuration of the illumination areas under the keys, such as individual per-key RGB or divided into multiple sections (e.g. 3-zone RGB).
Indicates whether the device features a dedicated hardware key to launch the AI assistant.
Type of operating system on a device e.g. IOS on Apple devices, Android for mobile devices.
The total quantity of individual battery cells used to power the device, including configurations with primary and backup cells (e.g., 1+2).
A measure of the charge stored by the battery. Determined by the mass of active material contained in the battery.
The maximum power output provided by the AC adapter, measured in watts (e.g. 65 W).
Indicates whether the product features a USB Type-C port specifically for charging purposes.
Indicates whether the device supports the USB Power Delivery standard for faster charging and higher power levels.
Holes on the edge of devices through which a cable lock can be passed, so the device can be locked to a desk etc.
The standard of the security slot used to attach a physical locking cable to the device (e.g. Kensington or Noble).
Indicates whether the device includes a dedicated microcontroller designed to secure hardware through integrated cryptographic keys.
The version of the hardware-based security chip used to provide cryptographic keys and ensure platform integrity (e.g. 2.0).
The environmental or ethical certifications the product has received to verify its sustainability standards (e.g., ASC or ACT Organic).
The measurement or extent of something from side to side.
The distance from the front to the back of something.
The height of the frontside of the product.
Height of the backside of the product.

Weight of the product without packaging (net weight). If possible, the net weight is given including standard accessories and supplies. Please note that sometimes the manufacturer leaves out the weight of accessories and/or supplies.
Indicates whether a power supply unit for connecting the device to an AC outlet is provided in the package.
The length of time the manufacturer guarantees the product against defects, typically expressed in months or years.
